_why: Render paths per motion block, for scripts/check-motion-part-render-paths.py. Curated by hand because which attribute set selects a different branch of a render.php is read from the code, not derivable from block.json (framework rule R-31-1 allows a curated list only as data with the reason). Each block is either `single` (the reason it is checked as one path by check-motion-part-selectors.py) or `paths`; a path's id is what block.json `supports.sgs.elements.<part>.absentIn` names. Contents are fixture inputs, never real client data.

accordion.single: One render path: its early returns (bail-outs, empty or editor notices) print none of the block's parts, and its branches only add or drop an element for its own content, never print a part's element under another class.

account.single: Its parts are printed by the logged-out tracking card and by includes/account/templates/dashboard.php, the logged-in dashboard (a WooCommerce template override reached through the WooCommerce shortcode); the harness renders no WooCommerce account endpoint, and without WooCommerce the block prints an editor notice only.

brand-strip.single: Its modes print mode-specific parts under their own names (brand-text in text mode, logo in logo mode, tile and name only with captions); no part's element is printed under another class in another mode, so the static check covers it.

buybox.single: Only the main path prints buybox markup, and it needs a Product_Manifest built from real variations, which the harness does not fake (scripts/qa/lib/wp-stubs.php, DELIBERATELY NOT STUBBED). The five fallback paths (no WooCommerce, not a WC_Product, a simple product, no manifest, a context over 24 KB) hand the page to core WooCommerce blocks, so no buybox part exists there by design.
